paindrawr 0.1.0

Add an RGBA raster array to a pain drawing based on spray coordinates

Source: R/pdr_add_rgba.R
pdr_add_rgba.Rd

Renders the strokes and spray points from one or more pain drawings into RGBA numeric arrays. By default, the array is attached as a $.rgba element to each drawing and the augmented drawing(s) are returned. Set rgba_only = TRUE to return only the array(s), each wrapped in a named list with a single $.rgba element. This is useful when assigning into a separate tibble list-column.

Usage

pdr_add_rgba(
  pdr_list,
  method = "memory",
  clean_up = TRUE,
  polygon = "none",
  rgba_only = FALSE
)

Arguments

pdr_list

A pain drawing in one of two forms:

  • A single drawing: a named list containing a .strokes element, as produced by pdr_import_json() or extracted from a list-column (e.g. pd$pdr_data[[1]]).

  • A list of drawings of any length, including 1 (e.g. pdr_example_data or a list-column such as pd$pdr_data).

method

Character. Controls the rasterization back-end. Either:

  • "memory" (default) — renders in-memory via ragg::agg_capture(), no temp file is written to disk.

  • "file" — saves to a temporary PNG via ggplot2::ggsave() and reads it back with png::readPNG(). Use this if the "memory" path is slow.

clean_up

Logical. If TRUE (default), the temporary PNG file is deleted on exit. Only relevant when method = "file". Set to FALSE to retain the file for debugging.

polygon

Character. Controls whether strokes are rendered as filled polygons instead of their original appearance. One of:

  • "none" (default) — pen strokes as paths, spray strokes as points.

  • "pen" — pen strokes as filled polygons.

  • "spray" — spray strokes as filled polygons.

  • "both" — both pen and spray strokes as filled polygons.

rgba_only

Logical. If FALSE (default), returns the input drawing(s) with a $.rgba element appended to each. If TRUE, returns a named list with a single $.rgba element (single drawing) or a list of such named lists (list of drawings). Use TRUE when assigning into a separate tibble list-column: mutate(rgba = pdr_add_rgba(pdr_data, rgba_only = TRUE)).

Value

  • rgba_only = FALSE (default): the input drawing (named list) with $.rgba appended, or a list of such augmented drawings when a list of drawings is supplied.

  • rgba_only = TRUE: a named list with a single element $.rgba, or a list of such named lists when a list of drawings is supplied.

In both cases $.rgba is a numeric array of dimensions height × width × 4 (RGBA channels, values in [0, 1]). Transparent pixels are set to black (RGB = 0).

Details

The output always has the same shape as the input: a single drawing returns a single result, and a list of drawings (of any length, including 1) returns a list of results of the same length.

Examples

# Single drawing: returns the drawing with $.rgba appended
drawing_with_rgba <- pdr_example_data$pdr_data[[1]] |> pdr_add_rgba()
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.raster(drawing_with_rgba$.rgba)


# Single drawing: returns list(.rgba = <array>)
rgba <- pdr_example_data$pdr_data[[1]] |> pdr_add_rgba(rgba_only = TRUE)
dim(rgba$.rgba)
#> [1] 500 450   4

# Render spray strokes as filled polygons
pdr_example_data$pdr_data[[1]] |> pdr_add_rgba(polygon = "spray")

# \donttest{
# Multiple drawings at once (a pdr_list)
drawings_with_rgba <- pdr_example_data$pdr_data[1:3] |> pdr_add_rgba()

# Tibble workflow
pd <- pdr_example_data[1:3, ]

## add .rgba to the drawings in the pdr_data list-column
pd |> dplyr::mutate(pdr_data = pdr_add_rgba(pdr_data))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   id                               pdr_data          sex      age duration  pain
#>   <chr>                            <list>            <fct>  <dbl> <fct>    <dbl>
#> 1 6d63804892233bbb18bc21bcf0d81d0d <named list [11]> Female  46   Chronic      6
#> 2 c8b12cd45d08e94241d4de9990d60f71 <named list [11]> Female  35.4 Acute        6
#> 3 25062ac7dbeb08d8b532ac474a7849ca <named list [11]> Female  38.4 Acute        5

## add rgba arrays in a separate list-column
pd_rgba <- pd |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    rgba = pdr_add_rgba(pdr_data, rgba_only = TRUE)
  )

## access the array for the first row
dim(pd_rgba$rgba[[1]]$.rgba)
#> [1] 500 450   4
